purpose: Seal the consumed-only N576-to-N192 IID white-field control and separate the numerical released-shell failure from the independent CF4 posterior-family failure.

interpretation.numerical_cause: On an even N192 output mesh, source frequencies +Nout/2 and -Nout/2 form one discrete output-Nyquist equivalence class. The legacy slice keeps one representative, after which the real inverse transform removes the inconsistent Hermitian boundary component. This lowers boundary power by about 17 percent.
interpretation.V8_L5_attribution: Only released shells 5--7 contain output-Nyquist boundary modes. Their boundary fractions grow from 1.86 to 10.58 percent, producing the same increasingly negative aggregate shell-power pattern as V8. The independent white control matches all three sealed V8 shell means within 0.00151 absolute power.
interpretation.repair_mechanism: Combining every source +/- output-Nyquist class with 1/sqrt(multiplicity) normalization preserves Gaussian unit variance and restores all affected aggregate shell powers close to one.
interpretation.scope_limit: This control explains and repairs the numerical L5 high-shell power mechanism only. It does not repair the L3/L4 failure caused by using 256 high-k variants of one fixed CF4 posterior parent.

next: Freeze and test a paired variance-preserving N192-to-N576 prolongation and N576-to-N192 restriction contract, including exact output-Nyquist round-trip identity.
